selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this warning at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It prepares readers by explaining why the book may be hard to understand and why people can still benefit from it.

questions.question: What should a reader still expect, even if the book is difficult?
questions.answer: A reader should expect to receive at least some benefit.

questions.question: How many reasons are given for why the book is difficult?
questions.answer: Five reasons are given.

questions.question: What is the first listed reason for the book’s difficulty?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own personal observations and understanding.

questions.question: Why might one sentence become very long in this book?
questions.answer: A sentence may become long so a large truth is kept whole instead of being broken apart.

questions.question: Which qualities of the topics are named in the second reason?
questions.answer: They are described as very broad, very deep, and sometimes very long.

questions.question: According to the passage, who may struggle with that many proofs?
questions.answer: People with limited understanding may find it hard to follow.

questions.question: What is the main complaint someone might have because of the fourth reason?
questions.answer: Someone might feel the discussion goes on too long because so many proofs are included.

questions.question: What three writing-related results came from the fifth reason?
questions.answer: The book was written quickly, not revised, and left with some Arabic parts, including one section moved into a separate work.

questions.question: What does the passage say about whether every reader will fully understand the whole treatise?
questions.answer: It says not everyone will understand all of it.

questions.question: What lesson about learning can be taken from the garden example?
questions.answer: A student does not need to master everything at once in order to benefit.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the purpose of the “garden”?
questions.answer: It is meant for many people, not just one person.

questions.question: What writing approach in the first reason may make this treatise different from more common books?
questions.answer: The ideas are expressed from the writer’s own way of seeing them, not adjusted to other people’s understandings.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about understanding deep topics quickly?
questions.answer: It suggests that such topics cannot always be understood all at once.

questions.question: In the third reason, why might a single sentence cover so much?
questions.answer: Because one sentence may carry a whole major truth without splitting it apart.

questions.question: How does the fourth cause differ from the third cause?
questions.answer: The third is about the size of each truth and the need for preparation, while the fourth is about having many proofs for the same matter.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying limited minds may not understand this?
questions.answer: Some readers may struggle to follow a discussion that is so full of detail and repeated evidence.

questions.question: Why did the writer think editing the text later might be wrong?
questions.answer: He felt the writing did not come simply from his own personal will, so changing it by his own later ideas seemed unsuitable.

questions.question: What final information about language and structure appears at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It says some Arabic sections remained, and the first section, which was entirely in Arabic, was separated into its own work.

questions.question: What does the passage say a reader should not expect before reading this treatise?
questions.answer: A reader should not expect that everyone will fully understand every part of it.

questions.question: What is the fourth reason the discussion sometimes feels lengthy?
questions.answer: Many topics have lots of proofs and evidences, so the writer includes many demonstrations.

questions.question: What physical and emotional struggles are mentioned in the fifth reason?
questions.answer: The writer mentions distress and several illnesses.

questions.question: In the second cause, what makes the topics especially hard to understand?
questions.answer: They are very broad, very deep, and sometimes very long.

questions.question: How does the fourth reason add another layer of difficulty beyond long sentences?
questions.answer: It says that many different proofs may be given for one matter, making the explanation even longer.
